# Software Requirements Specification

*Generated by the requirements-refinement agentic network on 2026-10-22 from 20 input documents.*

## 1. Introduction

This document consolidates the requirements found in the input corpus. Each requirement has a unique identifier `REQ-<AREA>-<NNN>`, a short name, a descriptive paragraph, a priority and the list of source documents it was derived from (see Section 2 for the document identifiers). Requirements that were identified but discarded are listed in the blacklist (Section 6) together with the reason; tensions between kept requirements that need stakeholder clarification are listed as open issues (Section 7).

### 1.1 Priority scale

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Must** | Essential for the system to be accepted. A source marks it as high priority, or states it as mandatory ("must", "shall", "critical", "essential", legal obligation). |
| **Should** | Important and expected in the first release, but a workaround exists; a source marks it as medium priority or phrases it as "should", "need" or "highly desirable". |
| **Could** | Nice to have; phrased as a wish ("would be helpful", "it would be nice") or requested by a single stakeholder without supporting sources. Can be postponed. |

Priority evidence is detected in the source text without AI: an explicit priority marker (e.g. `[* High Priority]`) in the paragraph of the quoted statement decides; otherwise the modal wording of the quote or of the nearest preceding sentence in the same paragraph. Statements without priority wording default to Should. A requirement can be Must only if at least one of its sources states it as mandatory, and an explicit high-priority marker always makes it Must.

### 1.2 Glossary

All requirements use the preferred terms below.

| Term | Definition | Avoided synonyms |
|---|---|---|
| Ad-hoc Query | An interactive, user-constructed query against reporting data allowing field selection, boolean/regex filters and immediate results for exploration or export. | one-off query, ad hoc report, ad-hoc report |
| Audit Trail | A recorded sequence of system events (who, what, when, where) used for forensic, compliance and change-history purposes. | log file, history, change log |
| Bibliographic Record (Bib) | The master metadata record describing a work (title/author/etc.); may be associated with zero or more physical copies/items. | bib record, bib rec, catalog record |
| Branch (Library) | A single physical facility or logical library location within a system/consortium; the principal unit of location-based reporting. | location, site, facility |
| Capacity | High-level view of space or holdings limits across branches or system; used for big-picture planning and threshold alerts. | cap, room, space limit |
| Copy / Item | A specific physical or electronic manifestation of a bibliographic record with its own barcode, status and location metadata. | volume, instance, piece |
| In-transit Item | An item that has been sent from one location to another and is recorded as en route until it is received at the destination. | on route, in transit (space), in-transit (verb) |
| Item Transfer | An operation that changes an item's owning or physical location (temporary or permanent), including associated status and transit tracking. | move record, relocate record, move |
| Last Copy | A bibliographic record for which zero copies would remain at the source(s) if a specified copy/volume is removed; used as a critical purge/weeding criterion. | last item, sole copy, last volume |
| Patron | A registered user of the library system with an account record used in circulation, holds and demographic reports. | user, member, customer |
| Purge | An intentional deletion process that removes records or items according to configured criteria and includes confirmation and audit logging. | delete en masse, mass delete, trash process |
| Queue | An ordered list of scheduled or running report jobs showing position, submission time and status; supports prioritization and cancellation. | job list, run list, report backlog |
| Report | A formatted output presenting selected data and aggregations, produced either on demand or on a schedule; may be canned, ad-hoc, or templated. | printout, sheet, run |
| Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) | A security model where user permissions are granted through roles and groups rather than to individual accounts. | role access, user rights, permission groups |
| Shelf Space | Estimated physical storage capacity used by items, expressed in units derived from item counts or item dimensions for collection planning and capacity reporting. | shelf estimate, space usage, shelving length |
| System (Consortium) | A grouping of branches/ libraries that share administration, data or services; reporting may be scoped at the system or consortium level. | network, region, group |
| Template | A saved, parameterized report definition that can be run directly or scheduled; includes field selection, filters, output format and permissions. | prewritten canned report, preset, report form |
| Weeding Report | A report identifying items for removal from the collection according to configured criteria (usage, age, condition, last-copy rules). | weeding list, discard report, weeding candidates |

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Collection & Capacity Metrics (COL)

Reports and analytics that describe the collection itself and physical capacity. Includes material volume and composition (by category, genre, format), shelving and shelf-space metrics, acquisitions and items inventory, location-based item counts, collection share, capacity views and trends (per branch, per system, and aggregate), data‑quality checks on bibliographic and item records (e.g., missing volumes, invalid item types, long call numbers), and configurable volume categories and groupings. Example topics: material volume reports, shelf items as source, new acquisitions as source, shelf space report, volume changes over time, collection share by genre/format, bib records with no volumes.

#### REQ-COL-001: Material Volume Snapshot Report

**Priority:** Should - All merged candidates are marked 'Should' or contain the wording 'should' in source material (e.g., C001, C184, C439).  
**Priority evidence:** D01: keyword "should" in the quote; D01: keyword "should" in the source paragraph; D10: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D01, D10, D15

The system shall provide a Report that shows the volume of material held by a Branch (Library) or System (Consortium) at a specified point in time. The Report shall use New acquisitions, Items on the shelf (checked in) and Items out in circulation (checked out) as data sources and present counts for common categories (for example: total Items, number of holds, adult fiction, board books). The Report shall allow selection of scope (single Branch (Library) or System (Consortium)) and basic filtering for reporting needs of collection managers and administrators. This capability exists to give immediate, point-in-time visibility into holdings for planning and operational decisions.

The report should allow breaking down volume in categories such as: total items in library, number of holds, number of adult fiction, number of board books, etc."
- **D15** `interview_cataloging_2009-05-08.txt`: "The material volume report helps me understand how much we have. I need to report on volume based on acquisitions, items on shelf, and items in circulation, broken down by categories like total items, holds, adult fiction, board books, etc."

#### REQ-COL-005: Shelf Space And Collection Share Report

**Priority:** Should - Both merged candidates are marked 'Should' or explicitly state 'should' in the source material (C186, C028).  
**Priority evidence:** D03: keyword "need" in the source paragraph; D10: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D03, D10, D15

The system shall provide a Shelf Space Report that produces shelf space information broken down by genre and by format and that, for each genre and format, includes the percentage of total Shelf Space, the percentage of total circulations and the percentage of the collection (the percentage of the bibliographic collection) and displays collection share percentages by genre and format to support collection balancing and space planning; the Report shall support comparisons between percentage of circulations, percentage of the bibliographic collection and percentage of Shelf Space and shall present the data in a way that supports identifying mismatches between use (circulations) and physical allocation so collection planners and branch staff can see how physical capacity is allocated. The Report shall be runnable per Branch (Library) and per System (Consortium), shall be available as a Report or Template for scheduled or on‑demand runs, shall allow scope selection and export for further analysis, and its output shall be usable by collection planners, branch staff and facilities managers to support collection planning and balancing and to inform reallocation and weeding decisions.

**Priority:** Should - All merged candidates are marked 'Should' or have neutral priority in source materials (e.g., C440–C442, C222, C223).

The system shall generate data-quality Reports that identify common issues in Item and Bibliographic Record (Bib) data, including Items with invalid Item Type, Items with long call numbers, Bibliographic Records with no Item records, Bibliographic Records with no Volumes attached, and Bibliographic Records missing specific MARC fields. These Reports shall support maintaining accurate holdings and improve downstream reporting quality.

#### REQ-COL-008: Last Edit Date Visibility

**Priority:** Should - The merged candidate (C443) is marked 'Should' or indicates need in its source material.  
**Priority evidence:** D15: keyword "need" in the quote  
**Sources:** D15

The system shall show the last edit date on Reports only when an Item has been edited and shall not use the last circulation activity as the last edit date. The display rule shall apply consistently across Reports and Templates that surface Item metadata to ensure cataloging and maintenance dates are not conflated with circulation events. This behavior is intended for catalogers and report consumers who rely on edit timestamps for quality and change-tracking purposes. The system shall document the rule so report readers understand the timestamp semantics.

- **D15** `interview_cataloging_2009-05-08.txt`: "I need to be able to see the last edit date on reports, but it should be only when the item is edited and not include the last circulation."

</details>

#### REQ-COL-009: Location-Based Item Count

**Priority:** Should - The merged candidate (C010) has source_priority 'Should' and contains wording indicating need in the source.  
**Priority evidence:** D01: keyword "need" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D01

The system shall count Items for volume Reports by counting all Items whose Branch (Library) equals the Branch (Library) being reported. The counting rule shall be applied consistently for point-in-time volume Reports, Templates and ad-hoc queries so that Branch-level totals are reproducible for collection managers and administrators. The capability exists to ensure that Reports reflect items physically or administratively assigned to the Branch (Library) used as the reporting scope. The system shall document how Items with transfers or in-transit status are handled relative to this counting rule.

### 4.2 Circulation & Transaction Analytics (CIR)

Reports and analytics about check‑out/check‑in activity, holds and hold workflows, loans (including inter-system/facility loans), renewals, transaction grouping and counts, transaction-level metadata (date/time/staff/workstation), return/turnaround metrics, fine/fee/payment reporting, and other transaction-based KPIs. Covers circulation counts by genre/format, percent renewals by branch, average return time, renewal likelihood, unfilled/stale holds, holds sent/received, intra-system loans, transactions per patron/library, detailed payments and voids, aged debt, and tracking of fines waived.

#### REQ-CIR-001: Transaction Grouping And Cross-tab Reports

**Priority:** Must - At least one merged candidate (C295) is marked Must (keyword "must"), so the consolidated requirement is Must; other merged candidates are Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "must" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D10, D15, D20

The system shall provide Reports and Ad-hoc Queries that allow grouping and cross-tabulation of transaction activity by hour, terminal/workstation, branch (Library), and system (Consortium), and by patron dimensions such as age range, patron type and patron home. The system shall allow filtering or drilling to specific date and time ranges and to transactions performed by a specific staff member or on a specific workstation. The system shall include traffic and volume metrics (check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, holds filled, fines collected, registrations) and support querying by all transactions or by transaction type and exporting results. These capabilities enable operations staff to analyze usage patterns and troubleshoot anomalies at the terminal, branch or system level.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "Transactions can be grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system. Transactions include check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, patron registrations, etc., and can be queried by all transactions or by type of transaction."
- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "Transactions can be grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system."
- **D15** `interview_cataloging_2009-05-08.txt`: "count transactions and include them in circulation statistics and reports."

</details>

### 4.3 Patron & Demographic Reporting (PAT)

Reports that describe patrons, their status and behavior, and outreach targets. Includes patron counts and trends (by age, profile group, home branch, county/city/zip), lists filtered by attributes (inactive, barred, expiring, specific note text), engagement metrics (OPAC/login/online holds/renewals/digital activity), survey and voter‑reg response rollups and lists, anonymization controls, exclusion rules, mailing-address outputs for outreach, and support for demographic and profile‑based reporting for outreach and program evaluation.

#### REQ-PAT-001: Inactive Patrons Report

**Priority:** Should - Merged candidates use the word "should" or neutral phrasing indicating this is a high-desirability feature for initial releases.  
**Priority evidence:** D09: keyword "should" in the quote; D09: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D10: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D09, D10

The system shall produce a Report listing patrons who have had no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days, where X is configurable. The Report shall be runnable at System (Consortium), Branch (Library), County and similar scopes so outreach or cleanup can be assigned appropriately. The system shall determine each patron's last activity by querying the transaction archive for the most recent activity and applying the X-day filter. The Report shall be usable for outreach and program evaluation workflows and shall respect exclusion and anonymization controls.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D09** `conversations/conv_pines024_inactive_patrons.eml`: "The system should generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days (X configurable)."
- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system should generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity in the last X days (X configurable). The list should be configurable to System, Home Library, County, etc."

</details>

### 4.4 Reporting Platform, Delivery & Compliance (RPF)

Capabilities and interfaces that enable, deliver and govern reporting across the system: canned and configurable report support, report scheduling and periodic reports, real‑time vs historical (warehouse/snapshot) delivery modes, selection and date‑range filtering, grouping and comparison views (per branch/system, local vs system average), configurable reporting levels (branch/system/custom levels), export/output columns, board and executive reports and cross‑tabulations, statutory compliance reports (e.g., Georgia Annual Report), report interfaces and testing/process definitions, and governance items (predefined report list, exclusion of patron‑facing functions from executive reporting, levels support).

#### REQ-RPF-001: Temporal Reporting And Comparisons

**Priority:** Should - Multiple sources describe these temporal/historical capabilities as needed or desirable (many candidates marked Should/Need) but none are explicitly marked Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D01: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D03: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D10: keyword "should" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D01, D03, D10, D19, D20

The system shall provide temporal reporting capabilities that let managers view and compare data across time. This includes date filters to view volume at a specific point in time, canned Report data windows (for example: yesterday, last week, last month, last year), and the ability to run snapshot/historical Reports from a reporting warehouse to view data as of a specific past date (for example: snapshot bills history going back in time). The system shall support output columns that show comparisons between time periods and percent differences (for example: last month, previous month, percent difference, previous year). These features will enable trend analysis and historical accountability for planning and compliance.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D01** `conversations/conv_pines014_material_volume.eml`: "date filters - volume at any point in time, not just current"
- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "Will have the ability for it to run by yesterday's data, last week's, last month's, or last year's."
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "Others are historical - 'what was the bill amount on June 30th?' We probably need a reporting warehouse for historical data."
- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "Historical reporting - I want to see what the data looked like on a specific date in the past, even if the shelving location has changed"
- **D03** `conversations/conv_pines016_shelf_space.eml`: "Can we also filter by date range? Like, what was the shelf space utilization in Q1 vs. Q2?"

</details>

#### REQ-RPF-002: Real-Time Reporting Support

**Priority:** Should - Several sources indicate real-time reporting is needed or desirable (candidates labeled Should and one labeled Could), so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D14: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D19: keyword "need" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D14, D19, D20

The system shall support real-time reporting so that reporting data can be delivered with minimal latency during busy periods. Real-time reporting shall be available as a delivery mode alongside historical/warehouse modes to support near-immediate operational decision making. The real-time capability is intended for high-traffic intervals and operational dashboards where up-to-date counts and activity metrics are required.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system provides a real time reporting" *(quote not found verbatim in source)*
- **D14** `evergreen_reference_2009.txt`: "Real time reporting - does not exist"
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "Some reports need to be real-time - like 'what's overdue today,'"
- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "Real-time reporting for busy periods"

</details>

#### REQ-RPF-003: Selection Criteria And Date Display

**Priority:** Must - At least one source explicitly states these items as mandatory using the word 'must', so the consolidated priority is Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "must" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D10

The system shall require clearly defined selection criteria for Reports and shall display the date selection criteria with the Report results (at the top or bottom of the output). Clear selection criteria and visible date-range metadata will ensure users can interpret results correctly and support auditability and compliance. This applies to both Ad-hoc Query results, Templates and scheduled Reports and must be enforced for all Report outputs. The selection metadata shall be included in exports and be visible to any authorized consumer of the output.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "Selection criteria is clearly defined"

</details>

#### REQ-RPF-004: Reporting Scopes And Levels

**Priority:** Should - Sources use 'should' and similar language to request multi‑level and comparison reporting, indicating this is expected for initial functionality but not explicitly mandated as Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D03: keyword "should" in the quote; D03: keyword "should" in the source paragraph; D03: keyword "want" in the quote  
**Sources:** D03, D09

The system shall support reporting scoped at multiple configurable levels so Reports can be run for a single Branch (Library), for the System (Consortium), and for other hierarchical levels such as County or custom administrative levels. The system shall provide comparison views that show each Branch (Library)'s breakdown side-by-side and shall support comparisons of a Branch (Library) against the System (Consortium) average. Configurable reporting levels and comparison views enable local managers and System (Consortium) administrators to analyze performance at the right organizational granularity. Level selection shall be available as a report parameter and enforced by permissions.

- **D09** `conversations/conv_pines024_inactive_patrons.eml`: "For the configurable levels - System, Home Library, County - that's just GROUP BY clauses. Easy."

</details>

#### REQ-RPF-005: Predefined And Fine-Grained Canned Reports

**Priority:** Must - Some sources explicitly use the word 'must' when requiring support for the referenced canned and fine‑grained Report definitions, so the requirement is Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "must" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D14

The system shall support predefined (canned) Reports and fine-grained reporting as specified in the referenced Report definitions. The system shall include a suite of predefined Reports such as Circulation Checkout Count; Circulation Renewals Count; Circulation Non-Cataloged Count; Circulation Count by Shelving Location; Items Added Count; Items Deleted Count; Items Currently Checked Out; Items Overdue by X Days; List of Items with Missing Status; Bib Records Count; Bib Records with No Volumes Attached; Patron Count; Patron Count by Branch (Library); Bills Currently Owed by Patrons; Detailed Payments Received; and Aged Debt. The system shall implement the detailed/fine-grained reporting requirements described in the specification appendices to support the predefined examples and other high-resolution reporting needs. Predefined Reports shall be runnable by authorized users via the canned Reports interface and capable of being scheduled as Templates where applicable.

#### REQ-RPF-006: Reporting Interfaces

**Priority:** Should - Sources describe the three-interface model as the intended design and label it as desired/expected (Should), so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D14: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D14

The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: Canned Reports, On-Demand Reports, and Open Template Reporting. Canned Reports shall run predefined Templates; On-Demand Reports shall support immediate Ad-hoc Query execution; Open Template Reporting shall permit saved, parameterized Templates that can be run directly or scheduled. Providing these interfaces will support both routine reporting needs and user-driven analysis workflows. Each interface shall respect RBAC permissions and reflect the administrator-managed Report catalog where applicable.

The system shall support scheduled (periodic) Reports that run automatically at configured intervals and deliver results for routine management and compliance tasks. Examples include bibliographic records with holds, Items that have not been checked out in X days, item-level holds, Items with invalid item type, Items with long call numbers, bibliographic records with no Item records, and Patrons with invalid Branch (Library). Scheduled Reports shall support parameterization of thresholds (for example, X days), delivery options, and retention policies appropriate for routine operations.

The system shall provide activity statistics such as traffic and volume of use (checkouts, check‑ins, holds placed, holds filled) and support cross‑tabulation by terminal, Branch (Library), System (Consortium), hour, age range, Patron type, and Patron Branch (Library). These executive‑focused Reports support oversight, funding compliance, and strategic planning.

The system shall support custom/local Reports that local administrators can define and run to meet unique local needs. Custom Reports shall allow field selection, boolean/regex filters, parameterization, and export so Branch (Library) staff can produce Reports tailored to local operations and reporting practices. #### REQ-RPF-012: Administrator-Managed Report Catalog

**Priority:** Should - The source requests expansion of Report types and frames this as an expected enhancement (Should); the candidate was marked Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D14: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D14

The system shall provide an administrator‑managed Report catalog that lets authorized administrators and report managers register, classify, and manage Report and Template types used across the reporting interfaces. For each registered Report type the catalog shall store metadata including name, identifier, description, parameters (for example date window, Branch (Library)/System (Consortium) scope, threshold values), default output columns, category/tags, and availability (enabled/disabled, deprecated). The catalog shall expose UI and API workflows for creating, editing, enabling/disabling and deprecating Report types; those actions shall be governed by RBAC and recorded in the Audit Trail with who/what/when details. Acceptance of this capability requires that an administrator can create, edit, change availability, and deprecate a Report type and that those changes are enforced in the Canned, On‑Demand and Template interfaces and logged for audit.

### 4.5 Ad-hoc Query & Report Builder (ADH)

Interactive query and ad‑hoc reporting tools including field selection, picklists, boolean and regex support, saved queries, manual selection from query results, pivot-style outputs and on‑demand exploratory reporting.

#### REQ-ADH-001: Include Null And Blank Fields In Results

**Priority:** Must - At least one source explicitly used the word "must" (e.g., C287, C543, C563), so the requirement is Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "must" in the quote; D19: keyword "must" in the quote; D20: keyword "must" in the quote  
**Sources:** D08, D10, D14, D19, D20

The system shall include all null and blank fields in Ad-hoc Query and Report results so that missing or empty values are visible to staff for accurate analysis and auditing. This applies to interactive Ad-hoc Queries and generated Reports regardless of active filters. The capability shall present nulls and blanks explicitly (not omit or collapse them) so counts and aggregations can account for missing data. This supports compliance, troubleshooting and correct interpretation of result sets.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results no matter what is being filtered or displayed"
- **D14** `evergreen_reference_2009.txt`: "All nulls and blank fields included in results - current system may filter some nulls"
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results,"
- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "All nulls and blank fields must be included in results"
- **D08** `conversations/conv_pines023_patron_characteristics.eml`: "Null values should be included in results"

</details>

#### REQ-ADH-002: Filter By Survey Name

**Priority:** Must - At least one source explicitly used the word "must" (C292), making the consolidated priority Must.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "must" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D10, D19

The system shall allow staff to filter Reports and Ad-hoc Queries by survey name without requiring staff to supply a survey identifier, by resolving survey names to survey identifiers internally. This filter shall accept human-readable survey names in the UI and map them to the underlying data store so users can run results by survey name. The capability shall work both in interactive queries and in Templates. This simplifies report creation and reduces dependence on low-level identifiers.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "Ability to select the survey name and not have to enter the survey id for filtering"
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "The ability to filter by survey name rather than survey ID requires the system to resolve names to IDs internally."

</details>

#### REQ-ADH-003: Pivot Table Output

**Priority:** Could - Sources described this as optional or desirable (keyword "could" / "would be great" in C284 and C560), so the requirement is Could.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "could" in the source paragraph; D20: keyword "would be great" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D20

The system shall provide pivot-style output (pivot tables) as an output format for Reports and Ad-hoc Queries so staff can perform cross-tabulation and multidimensional summarization on demand. The pivot output shall allow choosing row and column dimensions and aggregations (counts, sums) for exploratory analysis. This is an optional advanced output aimed at power users and analysts who need quick cross-tab views without exporting to external tools. It complements other output formats such as CSV and printable Reports.

**Priority:** Should - Sources used wording such as "needs" or "should" (e.g., C038, C423, C571), so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D04: keyword "needs" in the source paragraph; D15: keyword "need" in the source paragraph; D20: keyword "need" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D04, D15, D20

The system shall allow staff to save Ad-hoc Queries and report definitions for repeated use, so commonly used queries can be rerun without rebuilding criteria. Saved queries shall preserve selected fields, filters, and parameters and be runnable on demand or used as the basis for a Template. Saved queries shall be accessible according to Role-Based Access Control so appropriate staff can reuse team queries. This capability reduces repetitive work and supports standardization.

**Priority evidence:** D15: keyword "want" in the quote; D20: keyword "need" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D15, D20

The system shall allow staff to manually select records (for example titles or Copy / Items) from Ad-hoc Query results so selected items can be acted on, exported or included in downstream operations. The UI shall support selection of individual rows and aggregation/selection actions (select all on page, clear selection, export selected). Manual selection shall apply to interactive Queries and to results presented by Templates or on-demand Reports. This supports workflows such as targeted weeding, notifications, or curated exports.

**Priority:** Should - Sources explicitly stated this as a desired behavior (keyword "should" or neutral wording in C175 and C340), so the consolidated priority is Should.

The system shall display the query/filter selections alongside the results so staff can see what criteria produced a given result set. The displayed criteria shall include chosen fields, filter expressions, AND/OR grouping and any uploaded filter inputs (e.g., barcode lists). This information shall persist with exported Reports or saved Templates so results remain reproducible and auditable. Presenting the criteria promotes transparency and reduces confusion when reviewing or sharing Results.

#### REQ-ADH-007: Ad-Hoc Reporting Capability

**Priority:** Should - Sources described ad-hoc and on-demand reporting as needed or expected (keyword "should"/neutral in C152, C265, C266 and related candidates), so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the source paragraph; D10: keyword "want" in the quote; D10: keyword "want" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D10, D12

The system shall support Ad-hoc Queries and on-demand Reporting on specific data subsets so staff can perform exploratory analysis without developer intervention. The capability shall include an On Demand Reports interface and an Open Template Reporting interface exposing attributes for filtering and display, and shall allow choosing which data elements to include in results. The system shall also support uploading text files (for example barcodes or identifiers) to filter result sets. This enables quick, targeted reporting across record types for operational and planning tasks.

### 4.6 Report Templates, Scheduling & Queue (TMP)

Report template creation, management and integrity (runnable templates), scheduling (recurring, ASAP, hourly/daily/yearly), report queue and prioritization, email delivery and recipient address book, and recurring report editing.

#### REQ-TMP-001: Report Template Creation And Management

**Priority:** Should - Priority is Should because multiple sources and artifacts explicitly used 'should' or neutral defaults for template creation and management (e.g., C143, C365, C262).  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D12: keyword "need" in the quote; D14: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D12, D14, D17, D18, D20

The system shall provide a report template management capability that allows administrators to create, store and manage Templates that are available to staff for running or scheduling. The system shall allow saving and reuse of Template definitions and include a predefined set of Templates delivered with the product; the system shall also support determining and creating Templates needed for PINES libraries. The system shall present management functions for organizing Templates (for example via folders or metadata) and for administrators to maintain the catalog of Templates over time. This capability is intended to reduce repeated manual work, ensure consistency across staff, and provide an authoritative set of Templates for the consortium.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "System administrators should be able to create report templates that are available to staff."
- **D12** `email_report_features.eml`: "Admins need to create report templates that are available to staff."
- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "Report templates can be created by administrators and run as-is or modified."
- **D14** `evergreen_reference_2009.txt`: "Ability to save and reuse report definitions"
- **D17** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-03-15_minutes.txt`: "Determine and create templates needed for all PINES libraries."
- **D18** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt`: "4. Determine and create templates needed for all PINES libraries."

</details>

#### REQ-TMP-002: Runnable Templates

**Sources:** D10, D12, D20

The system shall allow Templates to be executed directly as-saved or to be modified prior to a run so staff can either run a Template unchanged or make temporary changes for specific needs. The system shall preserve the original Template while allowing one-time parameter or filter adjustments for the run. This flexibility shall apply to Templates created by administrators and to Templates saved by staff for reuse. This feature reduces friction for common reporting tasks while keeping canonical Templates intact.

#### REQ-TMP-003: Template Integrity And Consistency

**Priority:** Should - Priority is Should because source statements explicitly used 'should' or neutral defaults emphasizing the importance of preserving result accuracy (e.g., C145, C321).  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D12: keyword "should" in the source paragraph; D12: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D12

The system shall ensure Template changes do not compromise result accuracy and shall enforce consistency so that the same criteria produce the specified named Report. The system shall protect canonical Template definitions so that named Reports remain comparable over time and across runs. The system shall include safeguards and validation to prevent inadvertent changes that would alter the semantics of a Template without explicit administrative action. This is intended to preserve trust in Reports used for decision making and compliance.

### 4.7 Export, Integration & External Interfaces (EXP)

Output formats (CSV, Excel, HTML), export/warehouse approaches, vendor and third‑party interfaces (APIs, WorldCat), printable labels and external system integration (including file upload/download and API endpoints).

### 4.8 Data Management & Purging (DATA)

Functions for identifying and removing records (weeding/purge), last-copy handling, delete/retain rules and criteria (time-based, activity-based, combined), confirmation steps, read-only purge reports, and safe batch processing for deletions.

#### REQ-DATA-001: Purge Identification And Criteria

**Priority:** Should - All merged candidates used medium-priority phrasing such as "should" or similar language (e.g., C191, C429), so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D06: keyword "need" in the quote; D06: keyword "want" in the source paragraph; D06: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D06, D10, D15

The system shall provide utilities and Reports to identify Copy records for Purge using customizable criteria so collection staff can safely weed holdings. Criteria shall include time-based rules (for example, in a status for X months/years), activity-based rules (for example, last circulated more than X days/months/years ago), explicit status values (for example, missing for more than X months, discard/weed) and logical combination of criteria using AND. The system shall produce Weeding Reports and Templates that apply those criteria and present candidate lists for review prior to any destructive action. The utilities shall support both Ad-hoc Query-style exploration and saved Templates for repeatable selection of Purge candidates.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D06** `conversations/conv_pines021_item_purging.eml`: "I need to identify item records to purge based on customizable criteria."
- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system should provide a utility and reports for identifying item records to purge, based on customizable criteria such as:   - An item has been in status "missing" for more than X months   - An item has status "discard/weed""
- **D15** `interview_cataloging_2009-05-08.txt`: "Weeding reports are my most-used report type. I need to identify items for purging based on customizable criteria."

</details>

The system shall identify and Report Copies that are the Last Copy within a specified scope so catalogers and collection managers can avoid unintended loss of unique holdings. The system shall support running these Reports on-demand and periodically to assist tasks such as WorldCat editing and catalog maintenance. The Reports shall include sufficient bibliographic and Branch context to act on flagged Last Copies.

### 4.9 Item Transfer & Relocation Utilities (XFER)

Tools for moving items/records between locations: queries for candidate materials, generate pull lists, manual and batch relocation, change-location fields, preview/undo of transfers, auto-revert rules and transfer permissions.

#### REQ-XFER-001: Item Transfer Utility

**Priority:** Should - C188 explicitly used the word "should" and C421 provided neutral support, so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D15: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D15

The system shall provide an Item Transfer utility that enables staff to transfer batches of items between branches for use cases such as mobile libraries, outreach collections, or just-in-time warehouses. The utility shall support discovery and selection workflows (ad-hoc queries and saved query templates), allow manual selection and batch operations, and provide mechanisms to effect transfers such as changing an item's branch/location field or generating pull lists. The utility shall support temporary transfers with configurable revert rules and record all transfer operations in the audit trail. This capability enables efficient large-scale relocations while maintaining holdings accuracy and operational accountability.

### 4.11 Audit, Compliance & Retention (AUD)

Comprehensive audit trails and retention support for actions (deletions, transfers, financial transactions), audit table design, retention policy enforcement, compliance logging (financial/audit), and denied-attempts tracking.

#### REQ-AUD-001: Audit Table And Trigger

**Priority:** Should - Merged candidates use wording such as "need" and "should" or had neutral default priority; no merged candidate explicitly required this as mandatory.  
**Priority evidence:** D06: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D07: keyword "need" in the source paragraph; D07: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D06, D07

The system shall record all purges and deletions in a dedicated audit table to support forensic and compliance needs. The system shall implement a database trigger (or equivalent mechanism) that writes each purge/deletion event to the audit table at the time the action occurs. The audit table shall include fields such as record_type, record_id, deleted_by, deleted_at and location, and shall record the deleting user's Branch (Library) and the timestamp of the action. This requirement ensures that purges and deletions are captured reliably and consistently for later reporting and review.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D06** `conversations/conv_pines021_item_purging.eml`: "Audit trail for all purges"
- **D07** `conversations/conv_pines022_deletions.eml`: "1. A trigger in the database that logs deletions to an audit table"

</details>

**Priority evidence:** D07: keyword "need" in the source paragraph; D07: keyword "should" in the quote; D07: keyword "should" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D07, D10, D15, D20

The system shall provide a report interface that queries the deletion/purge audit table and produces counts and aggregations for operational and compliance review. Reports shall show deletions per Branch (Library) and per System (Consortium), support totals per period (month, quarter, year), and provide breakdowns by record type (for example: Item, Patron, other). The reporting functions shall allow aggregation and filtering by date range, by user, and by record type, and shall identify top deleting users and record deletion reasons where captured. The report interface shall support use on demand and for scheduled runs to support auditing and collection-management workflows.

### 4.12 Security & Access Control (SEC)

Role-based access control, roles and groups administration, fine-grained permissions for reports and templates, staff versus admin roles, OPAC/non‑OPAC access distinctions, and login methods (card/password).

#### REQ-SEC-001: Role-Based Access Control

**Priority:** Must - At least one source (C131) explicitly marked this as high priority with a high-priority marker.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: explicit marker "[* High Priority]"  
**Sources:** D10, D13, D16, D18, D19

The system shall implement Role-Based Access Control using security groups and roles so that user rights and privileges are granted through role and group membership rather than only to individual accounts. The system shall support RBAC assignments and permission evaluation for individual accounts, workgroups, and administrator-defined staff groups, and shall compute a user's effective permissions by aggregating grants and denials from all memberships. The system shall provide configurable, deterministic conflict-resolution or precedence rules (for example explicit-deny precedence or a role-precedence table) so that when a staff member belongs to multiple groups the resulting permissions are predictable and auditable. Administrators shall be able to create, manage and assign roles and groups consistently across system functions to support centralized permission management and scalable administration.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups and or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups."
- **D13** `email_staff_login.eml`: "we need user rights and privileges to be controlled through security groups and/or "roles"."
- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "The permission system needs to be controlled through security groups and/or 'roles.'"
- **D18** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt`: "CO-4: User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups and/or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups."
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "We need security groups and/or 'roles' that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups."

</details>

#### REQ-SEC-002: Role Administration Usability

**Priority:** Should - Sources consistently use 'should' or similar language indicating this is important but not explicitly mandatory.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D13: keyword "should" in the quote; D16: keyword "needs" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D13, D16

The system shall provide easy-to-use administration for roles and permissions so that changing a staff member's permissions is accomplished chiefly by changing their role assignment rather than by editing many individual permissions. The administration interface shall make common tasks (create, rename, assign, deactivate roles) straightforward for administrators and reduce the risk of inconsistent individual-permission edits. The feature shall support bulk assignment and simple workflows for routine role changes to minimize administrative overhead. This requirement exists to keep role management efficient and maintainable across branches and the system.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "All permissions should be easy to administer."
- **D13** `email_staff_login.eml`: "The system should make it easy to administer these roles - changing someone's permissions should be a simple matter of changing their role assignment, not modifying individual permissions."
- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "The system needs to make it easy to administer these roles."

</details>

#### REQ-SEC-003: Automatic Permission Updates

**Priority:** Should - Sources phrase this as a needed or desirable behavior ('need'/'should') indicating medium priority.  
**Priority evidence:** D12: keyword "need" in the quote; D16: keyword "should" in the quote; D19: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D12, D16, D19

The system shall automatically update a user's effective permissions when their role assignment changes so that permission changes take immediate effect without manual per-user edits. This automatic update shall include Report- and Template-related permissions so Reports and Templates available to the user reflect current role membership. The feature shall support role reassignment workflows (single change or bulk changes) and ensure consistency between role definitions and user privileges. This requirement exists to avoid stale or inconsistent permissions after role changes.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D12** `email_report_features.eml`: "The permissions need to be easy to administer. If I change someone from "Staff" to "Manager," their report permissions should update automatically based on the role."
- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "Changing someone's permissions should be a simple matter of changing their role assignment."
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "The system should make it easy to change someone's permissions by simply changing their role assignment."

</details>

#### REQ-SEC-004: Fine-Grained Report And Template Permissions

**Priority:** Should - Multiple sources describe this as 'should' or express the need for fine-grained control; no source made it explicitly mandatory.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D12: keyword "need" in the quote; D14: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D12, D14, D20

The system shall provide fine-grained permission levels governing creation, cloning, modification, scheduling and execution of Reports and Templates so that administrators can limit who may create, clone or run each Report or Template. The system shall allow restriction of which filters and filter values staff may apply when running Reports or Ad-hoc Queries, and shall control Template management separately from Report execution. Staff shall be able to run only the Reports they have access to, and administrators shall be able to assign distinct permissions for create/modify versus run/export. This requirement exists to protect sensitive data, enforce separation of duties, and allow tiered reporting capabilities across roles.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system should provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit who can create and clone reports."
- **D12** `email_report_features.eml`: "The permissions need to be easy to administer. If I change someone from "Staff" to "Manager," their report permissions should update automatically based on the role."

The system shall support streamlined staff login via card swipe (for example an RFID badge) and traditional login via individual username and password, with fallback to username/password for staff without ID cards; card-swipe login shall not bypass individual authentication and shall be tied to an identifiable staff account (card-to-account binding) and the system shall enforce any required secondary checks. Streamlined login methods shall be optional and configurable so branches may enable or disable card login, and the system shall be usable at branches that do not have card-reader infrastructure by providing an optional streamlined login mode for such sites. The system shall support a set of predefined role classes and associated capability examples—such as Patron, Staff, Front Desk Staff, Department Head, Library Manager, Library Director, Local System Administrator and Global System Administrator—so that common organizational responsibilities are represented out of the box. The system shall map typical permissions to these role classes (for example, Front Desk Staff may run basic Reports with limited filters; Department Heads may create and modify Templates; System Administrators and Global Admins have progressively broader configuration and reporting privileges; Patron access is indirect via OPAC displays). Administrators shall be able to customize these predefined roles or create additional roles as needed. This requirement exists to accelerate deployment and provide sensible default permission sets aligned to organizational needs.

### 4.13 System Architecture, Performance & Scalability (SYS)

Server and infrastructure constraints (supported OS, browsers), relational DB backend requirements, background processing and caching, performance for large datasets, scaling to many locations, separate reporting DB/warehouse options, and deployment environments (dev/training/production).

#### REQ-SYS-001: Consortium Scale Support

**Priority:** Must - At least one source explicitly marked this as High Priority or used mandatory wording (e.g. "[* High Priority]", "must").  
**Priority evidence:** D10: explicit marker "[* High Priority]"; D18: keyword "must" in the quote  
**Sources:** D02, D10, D18  
**Open issues:** OI-010 (see Section 7)

The system shall support operation for a large library consortium, including up to 286 branches, about 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing/processing over 900,000 items per year. This capability is required so administrators and planners can run management reports and capacity calculations across the full consortium workload. The system shall be designed to store and display capacity and circulation metrics at scale and to absorb the peak reporting and processing load implied by these volumes. Performance and sizing guidance shall reflect these numeric scale targets.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing/processing over 900,000 items per year."
- **D18** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt`: "Specifically, the system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, purchasing and processing over 900,000 items per year."
- **D02** `conversations/conv_pines015_capacity_interface.eml`: "Robert will look into technical constraints around displaying 286 locations."

</details>

#### REQ-SYS-002: Central Consolidation

**Priority:** Should - Sources used neutral or medium-priority wording (no explicit high-priority markers; several noted this as needed/should).  
**Priority evidence:** D02: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D10: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D18: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D02, D10, D18, D19

The system shall be consolidated at a central location and accept input and provide services to multiple branches, and shall store capacity data in a centralized database to enable aggregate queries across all branches. Central consolidation enables consistent management processes, centralized reporting and single-point administration for the consortium. The central store shall support queries and displays across all branches (up to the consortium scale) and be accessible for reporting and management processes.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D02** `conversations/conv_pines015_capacity_interface.eml`: "The data is centralized in our database, so we can build queries that aggregate across all branches."

#### REQ-SYS-012: Large Dataset Performance

**Priority:** Could - The originating source used wishful phrasing ("could"), indicating this is a nice-to-have that can be deferred; the source_priority was Could.  
**Priority evidence:** D09: keyword "could" in the quote  
**Sources:** D09

The system shall provide measurable performance for large datasets (as an optional capability): it shall support interactive Ad-hoc Queries over a patron dataset representative of consortium scale (up to 5 million patron records) returning the first result page (up to 100 rows) within 5 seconds 95% of the time under nominal load, and it shall complete scheduled Report aggregations over full-year circulation data (on the order of 17 million circulation events) within 60 minutes when executed as a background job. The system shall support at least 10 concurrent interactive Ad-hoc Queries with 95th-percentile latency under 10 seconds and shall be able to export 1 million rows within 30 minutes. The system shall achieve these targets using mechanisms such as background processing, query pagination, appropriate indexing, caching or materialized aggregates, and parallel execution; materialized structures for scheduled Reports may reside in a reporting warehouse or replica. Acceptance shall be demonstrated by reproducible performance tests against production-like datasets and test harnesses that report percentile latencies, throughput and resource consumption; meeting the stated metrics constitutes the acceptance criteria for this capability.

**Sources:** D10, D16, D18, D19

The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML output for its web-based components that validates against W3C standards. The HTML output shall use proper semantic markup and include ARIA labels where appropriate to expose semantics to assistive technologies. The HTML shall be tested for compatibility across supported browsers and with assistive technologies so that pages render and behave consistently. Validation results and any exceptions shall be recorded and available to developers for remediation.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system must produce standards-compliant HTML output for web-based components."
- **D19** `meeting_tech_subcommittee_2009-06-30.txt`: "The system must produce standards-compliant HTML."
- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "HTML output needs to be properly structured with alt tags, ARIA labels, and proper semantic HTML."
- **D18** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt`: "CO-2: Management Processes shall produce standards-compliant HTML."

</details>

#### REQ-UI-004: Section 508 Compliance

**Priority:** Must - Must because the source for C448 explicitly used the word "MUST" to state this requirement.  
**Priority evidence:** D16: keyword "MUST" in the quote  
**Sources:** D16

The system shall comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements so that it meets applicable legal and procurement accessibility obligations. Compliance shall cover user-facing screens, report interfaces, online help and administrative front-ends. The system shall provide evidence of compliance (test results, conformance statements) to support procurement and accessibility reviews. Any deviations from Section 508 shall be documented along with planned mitigation or compensating controls.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "MUST comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements."

</details>

#### REQ-UI-005: Assistive Technology Support

**Priority:** Must - Must because some merged sources (C126 and C490) explicitly use the keyword "shall" and are marked High Priority for assistive technology accessibility.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: explicit marker "[* High Priority]"; D18: keyword "shall" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D14, D16, D18

The system shall be accessible with assistive technology including screen-reading software (for example JAWS and NVDA), screen-magnification software (for example ZoomText), and other accessibility utilities so that users with disabilities can perform tasks. This support shall include the report interface as well as general UI workflows and shall be validated during acceptance testing. The system shall expose sufficient semantics (labels, roles, keyboard focus order) to ensure compatibility with these technologies. Accessibility limitations and recommended workarounds shall be documented for administrators and support staff.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system must be accessible with screen-reading software, screen- magnification software, and other assistive technology programs designed to increase accessibility."
- **D16** `interview_sysadmin_2009-05-10.txt`: "The system needs to work with:   - Screen readers like JAWS and NVDA"
- **D18** `meeting_minutes/meeting_2009-07-20_minutes.txt`: "Management Processes shall be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other software programs designed to increase accessibility."
- **D14** `evergreen_reference_2009.txt`: "No accessibility support for report interface"

</details>

#### REQ-UI-006: Searchable Online HTML Help

**Priority:** Must - Must because multiple sources (e.g., C135, C498, C529) explicitly state the help system "shall" be provided.

**Sources:** D10, D14, D16, D18, D19

The system shall provide an online, hierarchical and cross-linked HTML help system that documents and illustrates all system functions and is integrated with Reports and Templates. The help system shall be searchable and easy to navigate so that staff can find procedural and contextual information quickly. Help content shall be organized hierarchically with cross-links, examples and screenshots where appropriate, and shall be maintained alongside software releases. Context-sensitive links from screens and Report pages shall lead users directly to the most relevant help topics.

#### REQ-UI-007: Error Reporting And Feedback

**Priority:** Must - Must because sources in the set (C136, C499, C530) use the keyword "shall" to require this functionality.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "shall" in the quote; D18: keyword "shall" in the quote; D19: keyword "shall" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D18, D19

The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback to end users and shall allow low-level, query-specific feedback for Local and Global System Administrators via the front-end interface. The system shall record errors to support troubleshooting and shall expose appropriate diagnostic details to administrators while presenting user-friendly messages to general users. Documentation shall describe the error reporting behavior and the mechanisms for administrators to access low-level query diagnostics and logs. Feedback mechanisms shall permit administrators to capture, annotate and escalate issues found in queries or reports.

### 4.15 Inventory, Collection & Weeding Metrics (INV)

Inventory and collection management metrics such as volume counts, shelf space estimation (by count and dimensions), classification categories, weeding reports, last-copy reporting, material value, share by genre/format, and collection development support.

#### REQ-INV-002: Shelf Space Estimation By Item Dimensions

**Priority:** Should - The source candidate used 'need' and was extracted with a 'Should' priority, so this requirement is medium priority.  
**Priority evidence:** D03: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D03

The system shall estimate Shelf Space using recorded physical item dimensions so planners can calculate capacity using real size metrics. The estimation shall derive Shelf Space units from item dimension fields (for example height/depth/width or thickness) on Item records and aggregate to Branch (Library) or System levels. The capability shall be usable for planning, reporting and threshold alerts tied to Capacity. The system shall allow this estimation to be included in Reports and Templates.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D03** `conversations/conv_pines016_shelf_space.eml`: "Shelf space isn't directly tracked in the database."

</details>

#### REQ-INV-003: Shelf Space Estimation By Item Count

**Priority:** Should - The source candidate was phrased with 'need' and was assigned a 'Should' priority in the source.  
**Priority evidence:** D03: keyword "need" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D03

The system shall estimate Shelf Space using item count as a proxy when item dimensions are not available, enabling quick capacity estimates. The estimation shall convert counts into Shelf Space units using configurable assumptions (for example average thickness per format) and allow aggregation by Branch (Library), genre or format. The capability shall be available for inclusion in Reports, Templates and capacity summaries to support collection planning. The system shall document the assumptions used for the count-based conversion.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D03** `conversations/conv_pines016_shelf_space.eml`: "or use item count as a proxy."

</details>

#### REQ-INV-004: Weeding Report Configuration

**Priority:** Should - At least one merged candidate explicitly used 'should' (quoted) or was given medium-priority evidence, so the consolidated priority is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: keyword "should" in the quote; D12: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D10, D12

The system shall provide configurable Weeding Reports that front-line staff can restrict by call number range and control displayed fields. Staff shall be able to set call number ranges as filters and add or remove display fields from a pick list so Reports show exactly the data needed for local weeding decisions. The Reports shall be run on demand or saved as Templates for reuse and support export for audit or operational use. The feature shall support staff workflows for weeding and preserve Audit Trail information for report runs.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "For example, front-line staff could set a call number range for a weeding report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but they should not be able to alter the template to display deleted items."
- **D12** `email_report_features.eml`: "Example: Front-line staff can set a call number range for a weeding report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but can't alter the template to display deleted items."

</details>

#### REQ-INV-005: Uncataloged Materials Inventory

**Priority:** Should - Source candidates used 'need' language and were assigned 'Should' priority, indicating medium importance for initial releases.  
**Priority evidence:** D10: no priority wording in source; neutral default; D15: keyword "need" in the quote; D15: keyword "need" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D10, D15

The system shall support inventory control and fast processing of uncataloged materials so branches can distribute and track high-turnover or disposable stock with minimal labor. The capability shall allow quick distribution workflows, record transaction counts for uncataloged Items, and include those transactions in circulation statistics and Reports for usage analysis. The system shall enable branch staff to identify how uncataloged material is being used and shall minimize required branch labor through streamlined processing steps. The feature shall maintain Audit Trail information for transactions on uncataloged Items.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "Ability to control inventory of uncataloged material, such as paperback books and children's board books. Support needed for:   - Quick distribution   - Minimal branch labor   - Ability to identify how the material is being used  Ability to count transactions and include in circulation statistics and reports."
- **D15** `interview_cataloging_2009-05-08.txt`: "quick distribution (we need to process these fast)"

</details>

#### REQ-INV-006: Item Value Reporting

**Priority:** Should - One merged candidate was explicitly marked 'Should' in source material, so the consolidated requirement is Should.  
**Priority evidence:** D11: keyword "should" in the quote  
**Sources:** D10, D11

The system shall provide a Report capability that calculates the monetary value of Items using value data stored on Item records so staff can assess collection worth. The core capability shall allow staff to run or schedule the Report and obtain aggregate and item-level value information for use in budgeting, insurance and collection decisions. The Report shall be available as a Template and support export for accounting or stewardship purposes. The system shall respect RBAC permissions for who may run or view value reporting.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D10** `early_draft_srs_galecia.txt`: "The system can generate a report of the value of items (based on data in item record) in the entire collection or a portion."
- **D11** `email_financial_reports.eml`: "Value of items report - staff should be able to get the value of items based on data in item records."

</details>

#### REQ-INV-007: Item Value Report Scope Entire

**Priority:** Should - The source candidate used 'want' phrasing and was assigned 'Should' priority, indicating it is an expected capability.  
**Priority evidence:** D11: keyword "want" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D11

The system shall support generating Item Value Reports scoped for the entire collection so system-level administrators and finance staff can obtain a complete valuation. The Report shall aggregate values across all Branches (Libraries) in the System and present totals and selectable breakdowns. The feature shall be runnable on demand or scheduled as a Template and include appropriate RBAC controls to restrict access. The output shall include summary totals and support export for external financial use.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D11** `email_financial_reports.eml`: "Value of entire collection"

</details>

#### REQ-INV-008: Item Value Report Scope Portion

**Priority:** Could - The source candidate was explicitly labeled 'Could' and used tentative wording, so this is lower priority (nice-to-have).  
**Priority evidence:** D11: keyword "could" in the quote  
**Sources:** D11

The system shall support generating Item Value Reports limited to a portion of the collection (for example by Branch (Library), call number range, genre or format) so staff can value subsets for local budgeting or reporting. The scope selection shall be available as filters when running the Report or saving a Template. The feature shall enable export of scoped results and preserve RBAC controls for access. The system shall clearly indicate which filters were applied in the Report output for auditability.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D11** `email_financial_reports.eml`: "This could be the entire collection, or a portion."

</details>

#### REQ-INV-009: Item Value Report Filters

**Priority:** Should - The merged candidates used 'want' wording and were assigned 'Should' priority, indicating these filter capabilities are expected.  
**Priority evidence:** D11: keyword "want" in the source paragraph  
**Sources:** D11

The system shall allow Item Value Reports to be filtered by Item attributes such as item status (for example longoverdue) and item type (for example DVDs in a children's collection). The filter capability shall be available when running Reports or saving Templates and shall support combinations of filters for precise subsets. The system shall apply RBAC controls to filter capabilities and include the applied filters in Report metadata for auditing. The filtering shall enable staff to produce targeted valuation outputs for operational decisions.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D11** `email_financial_reports.eml`: "Value of all items with status "longoverdue""

</details>

#### REQ-INV-010: Collection Development Custom Reports

**Priority:** Should - The source candidate lacked explicit high-priority wording but was categorized as 'Should' in extraction, indicating medium priority for inclusion.  
**Priority evidence:** D20: no priority wording in source; neutral default  
**Sources:** D20

The system shall support collection development Reports provided as a customizable Report type so selectors and managers can create tailored analyses. The capability shall allow staff to save Templates with chosen fields, filters and output formats specific to collection development workflows and schedule those Templates for regular runs. The Reports shall support aggregation by Branch (Library), genre, format and other bibliographic or Item attributes commonly used in development decisions. The system shall enforce RBAC so only authorized roles can create or modify collection development Templates.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- **D20** `survey_results_2009.txt`: "Among those who use custom reports, the most common are: - Collection development reports"

</details>
