### 6.1 Merged duplicates

Requirements merged into another one because they express the same need. Their sources are attached to the requirement they were merged into; where both had distinct details, the texts were fused so that no detail is lost.

| Removed | Merged into | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-INV-001 Shelf Space By Genre/Format | REQ-COL-005 | Both require a shelf-space report broken down by genre and format that compares the collection’s shelf-space share with circulation and collection shares for planning. REQ-INV-001 adds scheduling and presentation details, but expresses the same core reporting need. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers the genre/format breakdown, shelf-space and circulation/collection percentage comparisons, planning use, and scope. However, the removed requirement adds distinct details not stated in the kept one: availability as a Report or Template, scheduled runs, branch staff as users, on-demand runs, and explicit support for identifying mismatches between use and physical allocation. |
| REQ-ADH-018 Demographic Filters And Age Handling | REQ-PAT-007 | Both require demographic filters for Queries and Reports using substantially the same patron attributes, exposed in Ad-hoc Query and Template interfaces. REQ-ADH-018 adds age-handling details, but the core demographic-filtering need is redundant. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers the listed demographic dimensions and use in Ad-hoc Queries and Templates, but it does not state that age ranges are configurable per report, that age or age ranges can be derived from the birth_date field, or that filters are usable in saved queries. These distinct details would be lost. |
| REQ-SEC-005 Shared Report Folders | REQ-TMP-007 | Both require shared report folders that govern staff access to Reports (and Templates) by folder. REQ-SEC-005 specifies additional permitted actions and role/group integration, but the core shared-folder access-control capability is repeated. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers shared folders, administrator-controlled run permissions, Templates and Reports, and sharing across branches or teams. The removed requirement adds distinct permissions to view, schedule, and modify Reports, explicitly distinguishes folder-level from individual Report permissions, and requires integration with role and group membership; these details would be lost. |
| REQ-TMP-016 Multiple Output Formats | REQ-EXP-001 | Both require support for multiple output formats for Reports and exports. REQ-EXP-001 adds specific format examples and export metadata, while REQ-TMP-016 adds format-selection and delivery details, but their core need overlaps. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers multiple formats, scheduled/on-demand exports, and specific reports, but it does not state PDF or other format options, format selection in Template definitions, consistency with selected display fields, or integration with email delivery and combined-run behaviors. Merging would lose these distinct details. |
| REQ-SYS-017 Integration With ILS Modules | REQ-EXP-009 | Both requirements express the need to integrate with an enterprise ILS, depend on its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, and document the integration points. REQ-EXP-009 adds further details, such as authoritative core data and modular deployment. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers the enterprise ILS dependency, Acquisitions/Cataloging integration, data reliance, and documentation, but the removed requirement adds distinct content: support for Management Processes, explicit data produced and consumed by those modules, interfaces with related modules, and simplified deployment for sites with full ILS stacks. |
| REQ-SYS-020 Card-Reader Optional Support | REQ-SEC-007 | Both require branches to remain usable without card-reader hardware and describe card-based login as optional. REQ-SEC-007 already covers fallback username/password login and branch-level configuration, making REQ-SYS-020 redundant. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers optional card login and username/password fallback, but the removed requirement adds distinct details: operation at branches without card-reader infrastructure, support for circulation and reporting workflows in those sites, and documentation of security or workflow differences when hardware is unavailable. |
| REQ-PAT-013 New Patron Count By Demographic | REQ-PAT-012 | Both requirements report newly added Patrons over a period, support monthly comparison, demographic breakdowns, filtering by Branch, and export. REQ-PAT-013 is substantially a demographic-specific restatement of REQ-PAT-012. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers monthly patron counts, demographic grouping, Branch scope, and exportability, but the removed requirement adds distinct details: administrator-specific filtering by other attributes, example demographic categories such as age or profile group, monthly comparisons, and use for program evaluation. |
| REQ-XFER-009 Time-Based Revert After Period | REQ-XFER-008 | REQ-XFER-008 explicitly requires time-based automatic reversion after a configured period, while REQ-XFER-009 repeats that same capability with only additional configuration detail. Texts fused so that the details of both are kept: The kept requirement covers time-based reversion and audit logging, but does not explicitly state that the period can be configured per transfer or as a global default, that individual transfers can override the default, or that item metadata is updated. |

## 7. Open issues

Pairs of requirements that pull in different directions but were not confirmed as irreconcilable by the independent verifier. Both requirements are kept; stakeholders should clarify the listed point before design. Explanations may mention identifiers of requirements that were later merged into the listed ones (see Section 6.1).

| ID | Requirements | Origin | What needs clarification |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-001 | REQ-RPF-011 Management-Focused Reporting Scope; REQ-UI-001 Web Or Windows Client Access | detector | REQ-RPF-011 excludes patron-facing functions from management reporting interfaces, while REQ-UI-001 describes staff and patrons using the system for tasks including reporting and administration. Clarify that reporting and administrative activities are staff-only, or identify which reporting capabilities are available to patrons. |
| OI-002 | REQ-ADH-009 Field Selection And Exposure; REQ-SEC-009 Table And Field Access Control | detector | REQ-ADH-009 calls for exposing the full set of reporting fields, while REQ-SEC-009 allows administrators to hide or restrict access to specific tables and fields. These can coexist if field exposure is subject to role- and administrator-defined access controls, but that exception should be made explicit. |
| OI-003 | REQ-TMP-006 Prevent Display Of Deleted Items; REQ-EXP-005 WorldCat Deleted Last-Copy List | detector | REQ-TMP-006 broadly bars Templates from displaying deleted items, while REQ-EXP-005 requires a report to list deleted last-copy items. Both can be met if the WorldCat report is treated as a dedicated deletion-audit exception, but that exception should be clarified. |
| OI-004 | REQ-TMP-006 Prevent Display Of Deleted Items; REQ-DATA-003 Deleted Last-Copy Audit Report | detector | REQ-TMP-006 broadly bars Templates from displaying deleted items, while REQ-DATA-003 requires a report listing deleted last copies. A dedicated audit-report exception can reconcile them, but the scope of the exclusion should be clarified. |
| OI-005 | REQ-DATA-009 Transaction History Retention; REQ-AUD-004 Retention Policy Enforcement | detector | Both govern retention of transaction data, but DATA-009 describes a configurable detailed-history window in days while AUD-004 requires retention periods to satisfy audit and legal policies, potentially for years. The scopes and effective retention periods should be clarified so the detailed-history policy does not purge records before applicable obligations are met. |
| OI-006 | REQ-DATA-009 Transaction History Retention; REQ-AUD-005 Transaction Archiving Privacy | detector | DATA-009 calls for detailed transaction history for forensic purposes, while AUD-005 requires archived transactions to be anonymized so they cannot identify patrons. These can coexist by distinguishing the detailed retention window from anonymized archives, but the transition and what forensic detail remains available should be clarified. |
| OI-007 | REQ-AUD-004 Retention Policy Enforcement; REQ-AUD-005 Transaction Archiving Privacy | detector | Retention for audit purposes and anonymization of archived transactions can pull in different directions if audit needs identifiable transaction details. Clarify which records and fields must remain identifiable, and which may be anonymized, so retention and privacy obligations can both be met. |
| OI-008 | REQ-EXP-001 Multiple Output Formats; REQ-EXP-007 Excel Export Deduplication | detector | REQ-EXP-001 calls for exporting Reports and data, while REQ-EXP-007 requires Excel exports to suppress duplicate rows. Suppression could omit rows that are legitimately part of a Report’s results. Clarify whether deduplication is part of the Report definition or a separately scoped export option. |
| OI-009 | REQ-EXP-006 Proven Output Quality; REQ-EXP-007 Excel Export Deduplication | detector | REQ-EXP-006 requires exported data to match the Report definition, whereas REQ-EXP-007 requires detected duplicate rows to be suppressed. These can pull in different directions if those rows are valid results under the definition; clarify whether validation is against the pre- or post-deduplication output, or how the Report definition accounts for deduplication. |
| OI-010 | REQ-SYS-001 Consortium Scale Support; REQ-SYS-008 Reporting Kept In Main DB | detector | Supporting consortium-scale reporting workloads while keeping reporting data in the main database may create contention or performance challenges. The requirements can coexist if the main-database mode is scoped to deployments where it can meet the scale and performance needs, with the stated mitigations. |
